title: Ranveer Singh Is Building India's First ₹300 Crore Zombie Film. He's Producing It, Too.
excerpt: After the Dhurandhar billions, the Don 3 walkout, and all the noise — Ranveer's next move is a post-apocalyptic Mumbai thriller with a South Indian star making her Hindi debut.
body:
The man who redefined Indian box office numbers is about to redefine Indian cinema itself.

**Ranveer Singh** — still riding the afterglow of the ₹1,400 crore *Dhurandhar* phenomenon — has locked his next move, and it'''s nothing like what anyone expected. No franchise. No sequel. No safe bet. Instead, Bollywood'''s most electrifying star is going full post-apocalypse with **Pralay**, a ₹300 crore zombie thriller that will attempt something no mainstream Hindi film has ever dared at this scale.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=ovYo6znkNPk</youtube>


Shooting begins in August 2026. The setting: Mumbai, overrun and unrecognisable. The tone, according to insiders, draws from *World War Z* and *I Am Legend* — survival cinema where a man fights through hell to protect his family. If the description alone doesn'''t give you chills, the budget should. At three hundred crore, Pralay will be among the most expensive Hindi films ever mounted.

> "Reports suggesting any uncertainty around Pralay are completely baseless. Ranveer and Jai have been in continuous discussions and have firmly locked the script." — Production source to Variety India

And Ranveer isn'''t just starring. He'''s producing. **Maa Kasam Films** — his newly launched banner — is co-producing alongside Hansal Mehta'''s True Story Films and Sameer Nair'''s Applause Entertainment. This isn'''t a vanity credit. This is Ranveer staking his own money, his own reputation, and his own creative instinct on a genre Bollywood has historically avoided.

## The Director Who Built Harshad Mehta

Behind the camera is **Jai Mehta**, the filmmaker who co-directed *Scam 1992: The Harshad Mehta Story* — arguably the most critically celebrated Indian series of the last decade — and went on to direct *Lootere*. The screenplay, co-written with Vishal Kapoor, has been in development for over a year, and the production is already deep into pre-production: location scouting, concept design, action choreography, and VFX planning that reportedly involves AI-driven visual effects to create a dystopian atmosphere "unlike anything seen in Indian cinema."

For Mehta, this marks his feature film debut. For Indian cinema, it marks a genuine genre breakthrough.

## She Conquered the South. Now She'''s Coming for Bollywood.

The casting that has the industry talking: **Kalyani Priyadarshan** will make her Hindi film debut opposite Ranveer. The daughter of legendary director Priyadarshan, Kalyani has already proven herself as a bona fide star in the South with the fantasy blockbuster *Lokah: Chapter 1 – Chandra*, which earned her nationwide recognition and a reputation for choosing bold, unconventional material.

Ranveer reportedly called Kalyani personally to convince her to take the role. She was initially hesitant — a zombie thriller isn'''t the obvious Bollywood debut — but after a long conversation about the script'''s emotional core and the scale of the production, she signed on. The pairing is unexpected, which is exactly why it works.

## Why This Matters for Diaspora Audiences

For NRIs who grew up on a steady diet of both Hollywood genre cinema and Bollywood masala, Pralay represents a collision of worlds. This isn'''t a low-budget horror experiment or a straight-to-OTT gamble. This is India'''s biggest box office star betting everything on a genre that global audiences already love — but executed through an Indian lens, set in Mumbai, with Indian emotional stakes.

If it works, Pralay doesn'''t just change Ranveer'''s career trajectory. It opens an entirely new corridor for Hindi cinema — one where genre filmmaking isn'''t niche, it'''s mainstream. One where a ₹300 crore zombie film starring a Bollywood A-lister isn'''t a punchline. It'''s a premiere.

The cameras roll in August. Mumbai is about to fall. And Ranveer Singh is betting he can save it.
